desk.headline: HEPS up 35% to 189 USc and adjusted EPS up 12% to 240 USc on Tencent, despite food-delivery spending; revenue up 55% to $6.4bn; Takealot breaks even

other.label: Media24 revenue
other.change: adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $11m from $9m

results: Revenue jumped 55% to $6.4bn (about R112.7bn), mainly from the Just Eat Takeaway.com and Despegar deals made through Prosus.
HEPS rose 35% to 189 USc and adjusted EPS rose 12% to 240 USc, lifted mostly by Tencent.
Adjusted EBITDA fell 6.4% to $405m as the group spent $344m building up iFood and Just Eat Takeaway.com.
The group swung to a $155m operating loss, mainly on a smaller gain from selling Tencent shares; EPS fell to 230 USc from 301 USc.
In South Africa, Takealot grew revenue 16% in local currency to $571m and reached break-even at the adjusted operating level; Mr D grocery sales grew 31%.

guidance.summary: Naspers' own outlook section could not be checked. Prosus, which holds most of Naspers' assets, expects profit and cash flow to improve in the second half as food-delivery spending eases, targeting a return to profit growth in FY28.

points: Naspers put Takealot's growth down to more orders and better conversion, calling it volume-led.
Grocery was singled out as the standout growth driver at Mr D.
Retail media (advertising sold to brands on Takealot) was described as an emerging revenue stream.
The group blamed the operating loss on a smaller gain from selling part of its Tencent stake.
call.source: Company statements quoted by TechCentral and BusinessTech (25 Nov 2026); Prosus outlook from the Prosus media release

watch: Whether Takealot can keep growing against Amazon Prime, which launched in South Africa in June.
Second-half profit recovery at iFood and Just Eat Takeaway.com, held through Prosus.
Tencent's earnings and dividends, which drive most of Naspers' earnings growth.
